items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: Even Bill Evans in my band, wasn't doing that. Bill Evans came up there, and he didn't like to play with one chord at all. That's why he split.

ctx.x: that's about ten years after I was doing it. He got an award from them. I got one, too, on the same piece, but my piece was written ten years before his. So I listened to Miles, I never heard him. It was just like the one I'd done, 'Blue Sea.' Either Blue Sea or -- one of those things that was on the album, 'Pithecanthropus Erectus,' where I used one chord.

I never felt confident with guys -- (inaudible) although the jazz did need some -- they were so hung up with playing, (inaudible) trying to play Charlie Parker, it was a good idea to come in with my one chord. Even Bill Evans in my band, wasn't doing that. Bill Evans came up there, and he didn't like to play with one chord at all. That's why he split. But then I wrote -- Brandeis University, when I did Revelations, I wrote it out for him. He had to do it. And he said, 'Man, I got to think about what you're doing.…

Well, after his ex-pause out there (inaudible) the kind of Blue record was really cause expose it to Bill, was the fact that Bill could do that very well, and was into all the modes and all that business of the scales.
